mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL growth reverts below 2% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE reverts to its previous level within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST growth reverts below 5% within 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO growth rebounds within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) shows an annualized growth rate above 3%, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy to combat inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or either FEDFUNDS falls below 4% or CPIAUCSL growth falls below 3% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points, signals a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the labor market indicators revert within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% over the previous three months signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth reverts below 5% within 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) shows a growth rate below 1% annualized and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% annualized, it signals a supply-side constraint, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO annualized growth < 1% and GDPC1 annualized growth < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or either INDPRO or GDPC1 growth rebounds within 3 months.
